note.p: Thomas Lovewell was registered as a bookseller and Stationer in 1802 and then again in 1805, with the latter being operated from Staines House in the Barbican district. In 1814 he published Lord Nelson's Letter to Lady Hamilton, but in December 1814 declared banrupcy - although this seems to have dragged on until 1817. It is possible that this is the Thomas Lovewell who had five chilren (John (1786) Charlotte (1787) Thomas (1788), Sarah (1789) and Charles (1793) - that might account for his bankrupcy!

Godwin is assessing him in some way (and it may not be Thomas, but one of the sons - or (less likely) one of the daughters) for some purpose in 1815. There is an intensive pattern of calling in July and September. It is possible he is using him as a middleman with the Shelley family. There is some connection with Margaret Jones and it is possible that subsequent appearances of M J in relation to Lovewell are relating to Margaret Jones rather than Mary Jane - and some of the locutions are odd! Perhaps most striking is the last enry when 'Lovewell calls, dernier fois' which is pretty much unique for the diary.
